It's remotely like Korean food.
Feb 2025 • Family
We came to dinner with the family. Looked at the menu, yes, it's more expensive than at local standard cafes/restaurants, including drinks, the cute look of the cafe, thought these guys knew their business for sure, asking for that kind of money and decided to stay! The order was: Seafood ramen; kimchi soup with tofu and soy paste; dumplings and barbecued beef marble. They brought the first beef, vegetables and sauces and a gas stove. Super quality meat, but on the menu 4 or 5 pieces in the photo, brought 2 pieces. I'm tense. That money was supposed to get you on the menu here, and then... Well, I guess all right, okay, so what's next? Among the snacks was Kimchi. Yes, everyone has different tastes, that's fine and proper, but I guess I'll be understood by those who understand sour Kimchie. I mean, it's fermented, it's just acidified. And I ordered kimchi soup, as you may recall. Brought me some soup. Very sour (because of the kimchi) and very salty. For the first time in a long time, I just couldn't finish the dish. The wife was brought the long-awaited Ramyong. That's the nail of the program! It was quick-cooking noodles from a tutu, with broth that had a little seasoning from this very industrial noodle added to it for VND 120,000 per serving. Son said dumplings were fire. I take it that if you're asking for 120,000-170,000 for a dish, when something like that from "neighbours" can cost 50,000-80,000, and beer, at its average price of 15,000-25,000 for 0.5 litres, and they're asking for 40,000, well, maybe part of that price should go to training chefs, staff, service and strict quality. And when you've just decided from the ceiling, "I'm an artist, I see that," and your paintings aren't Rembrant, that's a joke. Anyway, it was a knock-up. The most delicious was the raw beef we fried, fresh vegetables, rice and water, the son said dumplings were fine, I didn't taste them. Oh, by the way, rice! It's served in Korean restaurants in a metal bowl with a lid on soups and other dishes, instead of bread. So when I opened the rice lid... anyway, it was thrown in there and not taken in by a pot. Man, when you serve rice, well, spend 15 seconds more, lay it down nicely, so you don't feel like you've got it sloppy in there - good luck! Well, that's the review. Unfortunately, they didn't.
